LESSON: OBSERVING AND ARTICULATING SIGNS (LISTENING AND SPEAKING) 5.1.1 ARTICULATION OF WORDS AND SIGNING VOCABULARY

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Shopping Suggested vocabulary to be signed shop, shopkeeper, market, supermarket
Topic 5.1: Observing and articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 5.1.1 Articulation of words and signing vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Observing and articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 5.1.1 Articulation of words and signing vocabulary, part of Shopping Suggested vocabulary to be signed shop, shopkeeper, market, supermarket in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why do we go for shopping? 2. Why should we pronounce words and articulate signs with correct mouth movement ?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Observing and articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 5.1.1 Articulation of words and signing vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: Listening attentively and observing keenly is enhanced as they listen to or observe audio-visual

recording/teacher model of the target letter sound combinations and pronounce and articulate the signs with correct mouth movement.

● Digital literacy: Interacting with digital devices as learners watch a video on shopping.

● Learning to learn: Independent reading skills as they practice pronouncing and articulating the sign with correct mouth movement of the target

letter-sound combinations correctly.

Values:
Responsibility: Self-drive as learners take up assigned roles and responsibilities during role play of shopping activities.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life Skills: Effective communication as learners use vocabulary learnt when doing shopping.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Learner is able to relate proper pronunciation and articulation of signs of words to their learning in Kenya Sign Language.

Suggested Learning Resources

Adapted course book, Chart, class readers, course books, flash cards, recording devices e.g. tablets, mobile phone, dictionary, internet, signed audio- visual recordings
